html:
Afghanistan is a mountain country between Central and South Asia, with Kabul as its capital. The map shows it from 1783 on, as a state that took shape in the 1700s.

Its land had long been a crossroads. Persian, Greek, Buddhist Kushan and Muslim rulers passed through, and the Mughal Empire began here when Babur took Kabul in 1504. The modern state starts in 1747, when Ahmad Shah Durrani united the Pashtun tribes and built an empire that reached into Iran and north India.

In the 1800s Afghanistan sat between the British Raj and the expanding Russian Empire, in the contest called the Great Game.

  • First Anglo-Afghan War, 1839 to 1842: a British army that had occupied Kabul was destroyed on its retreat.
  • Second Anglo-Afghan War, 1878 to 1880: Britain took control of Afghan foreign policy.
  • 1893: the Durand Line fixed the border with British India and split the Pashtuns.
  • 1919: after a third war, full independence.

The kingdom was quiet for decades under Zahir Shah, who gave it a new constitution in 1964. A coup ended the monarchy in 1973, communists took power in 1978, and the Soviet invasion of 1979 began a war that drove millions abroad as refugees. After the Soviets left in 1989, civil war brought the Taliban to power in 1996. A US-led coalition removed them in 2001. They returned in August 2021 and rule again.
sum: Afghanistan is a mountain country between Central and South Asia, with Kabul as its capital. The map shows it from 1783 on, as a state that took shape in the 1700s.
